findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion with a test that drives byte_total above the cap and asserts _gc_pass evicts a tickets- entry (trigger fires end-to-end), not only that byte_total is accounted.
evidence: AC-3: 'A test observes the untracked bytes RED ... and GREEN after the fix' — this exercises accounting only
AC-1 introduces the byte-total-driven trigger but no criterion exercises _gc_pass evicting when byte_total > cap
findings.finding: No acceptance criterion proves the new eviction trigger actually fires and reclaims when byte_total exceeds the cap; AC-3 only observes byte_total accounting (the AC-2 fix), not that AC-1's trigger evicts.
scenarios: Accounting is fixed (byte_total correct) but the _gc_pass cap branch has a bug and never evicts; all listed ACs still pass green
findings.suggested_fix: Add: 'A test constructs a store whose byte_total exceeds the configured cap and asserts _gc_pass removes evictable entries until byte_total is under the cap.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion for a test that drives byte_total past the configured cap and asserts _gc_pass evicts entries down below the cap (the new trigger fires end-to-end), not just that bytes are accounted.
evidence: AC #1 'gains a byte-total-driven eviction trigger with a documented, configurable cap'
AC #3 only 'observes the untracked bytes RED ... and GREEN' — it validates accounting, not that the cap trigger fires and reclaims
the plan notes _is_entry already recognises tickets- entries as evictable 'so GC would remove them if a trigger ever fired' — the trigger is the new logic, so it needs a firing test
findings.finding: AC #3 tests only the accounting (untracked bytes RED/GREEN) but no acceptance criterion exercises the NEW eviction trigger itself — i.e. a test that, once byte_total exceeds the configured cap, _gc_pass actually evicts entries. The plan adds conditional eviction logic (a new trigger) whose behavior is never proven by construction.

findings.checklist_item: Specify that materialize_tickets calls add_bytes(entry_size(dest)) ONLY on the successful-rename (populate-winner) branch — the `else` after os.rename succeeds — never in the lost-race branch, mirroring cache.acquire's exactly-once accounting under single-flight.
evidence: cache.acquire reaches add_bytes only as the populate winner because it holds interprocess_lock (cache.py:195-203): '# We performed the populate — account its bytes exactly once.'

materialize_tickets has an explicit lost-race branch: 'Another materialization won the race (same SHA == same content); keep theirs.' with shutil.rmtree(build) (repo_snapshot.py:695-697) and takes NO interprocess_lock around build->rename
If add_bytes(entry_size(dest)) is placed after the try-block, both the rename winner AND the lost-race loser would add the same entry's bytes → over-counting drift
findings.finding: The plan does not specify WHERE in materialize_tickets add_bytes must be called, and a naive placement double-counts on the lost-race branch because materialize_tickets (unlike cache.acquire) has no single-flight lock guaranteeing exactly-once accounting.
findings.location: AC line: 'materialize_tickets records its entries in the store's byte total'; repo_snapshot.py:681-702
scenarios: Two processes materialize the same tickets-<sha> concurrently; the loser rmtree's its build but still adds ~620 MiB to byte_total, permanently inflating the total and prematurely tripping the new cap
findings.suggested_fix: Place add_bytes(entry_size(dest), store) in the `else:` clause of the os.rename try/except (after _fsync_dir(dest.parent)), so only the process that actually created the entry accounts its bytes — matching cache.acquire's exactly-once semantics.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: Specify how the byte-cap trigger integrates with the existing _gc_pass LRU loop — its armed condition (byte_total > cap), its stop/hysteresis target, and how it combines with the existing need_space/too_cold eviction predicate.
evidence: _gc_pass's loop evicts while `need_space or too_cold`, with hysteresis via `need_space = need_space and free < target` (janitor.py:402-413)

A byte-cap trigger needs an analogous armed/disarmed condition (evict LRU until byte_total drops under the cap, likely with a target/hysteresis margin) or it will thrash one entry per pass like the free-space term the module deliberately avoids
The plan states the outcome ('gains a trigger with a configurable cap') but not the loop-integration/stop-condition
findings.finding: The plan does not specify how the new byte-total cap trigger composes with _gc_pass's existing LRU victim loop and free-space hysteresis (need_space/target), leaving the stop condition for cap-driven eviction unspecified.
findings.location: AC line: '_gc_pass gains a byte-total-driven eviction trigger'; janitor.py:377-416
scenarios: Cap is exceeded by a small margin; without a hysteresis target the pass evicts exactly one entry, re-fires next interval, and thrashes — the exact failure RECLAIM_TARGET_MARGIN_PCT was added to prevent for the free-space term

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the cap knob's config-key name and its default value (and a one-line rationale tying the default to a reclaim goal, e.g. relative to the ~620 MiB tickets entries).
evidence: 'a byte-total-driven eviction trigger with a documented, configurable cap'
AC-4 references 'the new cap knob' with no name or default value given
the cap is a threshold asserted-not-derived; no default stated for the executor
findings.finding: The new cap knob's default value and config-key name are unspecified; AC-1 says 'configurable cap' but never states the default or how it is chosen.
scenarios: Executor must invent a default cap value and a config key name, risking a value that never fires on the review-bot volume the plan cites
findings.suggested_fix: Name the knob (e.g. `snapshot.store_cap_bytes` / `REBAR_SNAPSHOT_STORE_CAP_BYTES`) and give a concrete default derived from expected store size (e.g. a multiple of the ~620 MiB tickets entry size).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that materialize_tickets' add_bytes is idempotent per tickets-<sha> (only accounts on first materialization / de-dupes against existing entries), so retries or repeat calls don't drift byte_total.
evidence: 'materialize_tickets records its entries in the store's byte total'

cache.acquire already calls add_bytes(entry_size(dest)) at cache.py:203, so two writers now mutate byte_total; the plan does not state whether materialize_tickets guards against re-accounting an existing tickets-<sha>
byte_total now drives eviction, so accounting drift causes wrong eviction decisions
findings.finding: The plan makes materialize_tickets a new writer of the shared, incrementally-maintained byte_total counter but does not address idempotency: if a tickets-<sha> entry is re-materialized (retry, or a second call for an already-present sha) add_bytes could be invoked twice, double-counting bytes and drifting byte_total away from real store size — the same class of drift the plan is fixing.
findings.suggested_fix: State that materialize_tickets checks whether the tickets-<sha> entry already contributes to byte_total (or reconciles via startup_sweep) before adding, mirroring acquire's single-add semantics.

findings.checklist_item: Justify the new cap knob against the existing free_watermark_pct term (state why a separate byte-total cap is needed rather than tuning the volume-relative percentage), and specify how the two triggers interact/take precedence.
evidence: docs/config.md:478 already defines free_watermark_pct: 'ALSO reclaim when free disk < this % of the volume; 0 = off' — a volume-relative term added (per JanitorConfig docstring janitor.py:104-108) precisely because the absolute floor is disk-size-blind

The Impact section frames the failure as the free-space trigger being 'unreachable below 93.3% used on that volume' — a tuning gap in the existing pct term, which does not by itself establish that a NEW byte-total cap knob (vs. raising free_watermark_pct) is the minimal fix

ADR 0005 D5 (docs/adr/0005-...:72-74) does promise the byte total as a distinct backstop, so a byte-total trigger is contractually grounded — the open question is only whether it warrants its own config key
findings.finding: The new configurable store-size cap knob may duplicate the existing free_watermark_pct volume-relative reclaim term; the plan does not justify why a separate knob is needed rather than reusing/tuning the existing percentage term that already targets reclaim-before-alarm.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria, lines 1 and 4 ('a documented, configurable cap' / 'the new cap knob')
scenarios: Operator now has two overlapping size-reclaim knobs (free_watermark_pct and a byte-total cap) whose interaction/precedence is unspecified
A reviewer or operator cannot tell which knob to set for a given deployment
